oliver: Heads-up — after the continuous-batching tweak landed we see an unexpected perf regression. p50 unchanged but p95 +130ms, and KV prefix cache hit-rate dropped ~12% :thinking_face:
anya: Oof. Do you have a small repro or a trace? My hypothesis: batch composition is mixing prefixes that used to be coalesced, invalidating more KV cache entries.
oliver: Pasted a short sample from yesterday's traffic where the new batcher prioritized fill over affinity.
oliver: ```
trace_id: abc123
srv: serving-03
reqs_in_batch: 40
unique_prefixes: 28
kv_hits: 31
kv_lookups: 52
p95_latency_ms: 420
```
maria: That unique_prefixes / reqs_in_batch ratio is the culprit. Kernel selection is fine; we're just losing cache reuse so more KV shuffles and some kernel cold paths get hit more often.
kevin: Agreed. Two levers: (A) bias batching towards prefix-affinity when queue depth < X, (B) increase immediate warmup budget for newly observed prefixes so first few requests don't pay full cost.
jon: We should be careful about queueing latency. If we enforce affinity we may increase tail queueing time. Maybe a hybrid: affinity-first up to latency budget T, otherwise fill-to-X.
perf-bot: Profile snippet (from last rollout):
```
hotspots:
  kv_lookup: 28.1%
  seq_attn_kernels: 21.4%
  io: 14.7%
  fallback_kernels: 9.3%
  batching_overhead: 6.5%
```
perf-bot: Hit-rate by cohort: default-cohort 0.78, new-batcher 0.66 (measured over 15m window).
sre-bot: Alerts fired at 14:12 UTC for p95 latency > 400ms on model-x. Noise reduced after 14:40 with traffic drop.
anya: Can we get a cheap metric: per-batch prefix-entropy + kv_hit_ratio. Then make the batcher log it and we can correlate decisions to hit-rate.
maria: Also check kernel selection churn. If a batch ends up having many short vs long sequences, we might flip kernel variants mid-batch which adds overhead. Not just KV misses.
kevin: Quick experiment plan: revert affinity=false change behind a flag for 1 hour on canary, measure p95 + hit-rate. If that recovers, we incrementally reintroduce affinity with a small queueing slack.
jon: Another experiment: keying strategy variant - current cache key = (model, prefix_hash, prompt_bucket). Try dropping prompt_bucket for cache key (coarser key) and see if hit-rate improves without quality regression.
oliver: I worry about correctness if key is too coarse. But we can A/B with synthetic prompt sets.
anya: Implementation notes: batcher has a reorder window W (ms). We can add a scoring: score = alpha*(1 - prefix_entropy) - beta*(queue_wait / W). Tune alpha/beta.
kevin: For warmup: allocate 2% of GPU cycles to eager KV warmup for new prefixes for first N requests; cheap and effective.
perf-bot: Proposed metrics to add: per-batch prefix_entropy, avg_prefix_group_size, kv_hits_per_batch, kernel_variant_switches.
sre-bot: Add alert if avg_prefix_group_size < 2 AND p95 > baseline + 50ms for 5m.
maria: I'll run microbench with synthetic mix (uniform vs skewed prefixes) to see sensitivity curve.
oliver: Action items: (1) anya to add logging + metrics (2) kevin to flag rollback toggle + canary (3) maria to run microbench and share plots by EOD (4) jon to prototype coarse key experiment. I'll coordinate testing windows. :thumbsup:
kevin: I'll queue the rollback patch and make it feature-flagged.
anya: Logged metric PR -> CI pipeline, will push in ~45m.
jon: I'll spin up the coarse-key A/B and attach evaluation harness.
oliver: Thanks folks — let's keep updates tight in this thread. If someone wants to pair on the microbench ping me.
